confidence_notes: I based the food and drink prices on four web searches of aggregated cost-of-living sites and travel guides. These included Nomad Watch, Nomadic Matt, Stamped Nomad, Wikivoyage, Mapsorted, Faroway, Travelstar360 and Sologuides. Their figures conflict, and some are from before 2026. One backpacker guide warns that older online prices for Laos understate current costs because the kip has lost value, so I leaned toward the middle-to-upper end of the quoted ranges for July 2026. Beer is based on Beerlao at about 20,000–50,000 kip in bars and restaurants. Coffee is based on a cappuccino at about 30,000–40,000 kip in tourist cafes. The inexpensive meal is based on about $2.50 (aggregator) and noodle or market meals at 30,000–50,000 kip. The mid-range meal for two is less certain because sources mix in drinks and Western dishes, and Western mains cost about 100,000–200,000 kip. I found no published cocktail or wine-by-the-glass prices. The cocktail estimate comes from the riverside bar 'sunset drink' range of 25,000–80,000 kip, the bar drinks range of $1–3, and a multiple of the beer price. The wine estimate is a model estimate that assumes imported wine costs about 2.5–3 times the price of a beer. All four accommodation prices are holistic model estimates from general knowledge only. I did not check booking sites or listings, and July is the rainy low season, which may lower the real rates.
comparable_city_reasoning: I treated Vang Vieng as a budget backpacker and adventure town in Laos. Its prices are a little below Luang Prabang and Vientiane but slightly raised in tourist-facing riverside venues. Similar towns elsewhere in Southeast Asia include Pai in Thailand and Ninh Binh in Vietnam.
